subject: Contract addendum: runtime scope — no-training request & subprocessor allowlist
messages:
From: Emma King <emma.king@sablethera.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-01-09T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Contract addendum: runtime training prohibition & subprocessor list

Hi Logan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — our security and procurement teams reviewed Redwood's standard DPA and have a couple of non-negotiable asks before we can move to counterparty sign-off:  

1) Absolute prohibition on using Sable customer data (including runtime prompts & logs) to train any model or for model improvement without explicit written consent and a separate amendment.
2) A defined subprocessor allowlist: Sable requires a named list of subprocessors that will access runtime payloads.
3) Residency for ephemeral KV/cache entries must be limited to the US-East region and purged within 30 days; any exceptions need prior written approval.

I've attached our counterproposal (sable-counterproposal_runtime_addendum.docx). Procurement is ready to sign quickly once you confirm acceptance of the three items above or propose acceptable alternative language.

Please loop in your product and security folks for technical confirmation.

Thanks,
Emma King
Head of Procurement, Sable Therapeutics

Subject: Re: Fwd: Contract addendum: runtime training prohibition & subprocessor list — legal redline summary

Team,

I've reviewed Sable's counterproposal and attached a redline (redline_runtime_addendum_olga.docx) with legal comments. Short summary:

- "No training" absolute language is customer-friendly but creates operational rigidity. Recommend: commit to "no use of customer runtime data for training, model improvement, or research unless Customer provides prior written consent via a separate amendment." That keeps commercial flexibility while honoring the customer's concern.
- Subprocessor allowlist: acceptable to disclose our known subprocessors and agree to an allowlist mechanism for customer-specific restrictions. We should reserve the right to add subprocessors with notice and offer a mitigation path rather than a hard veto.
- KV/cache residency & purge: we can reasonably guarantee region-limited ephemeral caches for most Hosted and Dedicated deployments, and a 30-day max retention is feasible for ephemeral KV if product confirms.

Risks:
- If product cannot strictly isolate caches per-customer (for multi-tenant shared pools) we need to avoid wording that suggests per-instance physical isolation.
- Auditability: customer will expect demonstrable logs/audit trail for any access to runtime payloads. Need to confirm retention window for audit logs.

Next: Product, please confirm the technical guarantees you can accept. If you agree to the proposed redline language, I'll prepare a clean addendum and route to DocuSign.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Contract addendum: runtime training prohibition & subprocessor allowlist — product feasibility

Hi all,

Quick technical take after syncing with Runtime/Infra: we can accept the following items with the enumerated caveats. I've attached a revised draft (runtime-addendum_v3.docx) with suggested wording.

Acceptable (we can commit to):
- "No use for training": We can agree to "Redwood will not use Customer runtime payloads (prompts, responses, or logs) to train models or improve models unless Customer provides explicit, separate written consent." That is operationally achievable — we already have flags to opt datasets out of training pipelines.
- Subprocessor allowlist: We can provide the current list of subprocessors and a process to request removal/addition. For Dedicated and Private deployments we can enforce allowlist restrictions; for Hosted we can provide contractual commitments plus mitigation steps and a security review for any newly added subprocessor.
- KV/cache residency & purge: We can guarantee KV/cache residency in the specified region (us-east) for customers who have a region preference and can set a 30-day TTL for ephemeral cache entries. Caveat: in cross-region failover events there may be short-lived replicas; will include language about "reasonable efforts during failover" and immediate purge post-failover.

Telemetry & Audit logs:
- We can provide audit logs for runtime access and surface them via the Console. Proposed retention: 180 days for audit logs (minimum) with options to extend via enterprise plan.
- Telemetry for product improvement: we propose aggregated, pseudonymized telemetry by default; no raw runtime payloads will be included in telemetry without explicit consent.

Suggested contract language highlights (in doc):
- Add sentence that training requires a separate Amendment and explicit opt-in.
- Define "Subprocessors" and an allowlist procedure; allow Redwood to add subprocessors with 30 days' notice unless Customer objects and reasonable mitigation is implemented.
- Define "Ephemeral Cache" with a 30-day TTL and explicit note about cross-region failover replicas.

If legal signs off on the redline language, Product is comfortable marking this as "business-acceptable". I'll sign off on product feasibility - we should still preserve the failover and shared-pool caveats.

Marissa Cole
VP, Product Management
Redwood Inference

Hi Emma,

Thanks for the clear asks and for the patience while we coordinated internally. Short summary of what Redwood can commit to:

- Redwood will not use Customer runtime payloads to train or improve models without Customer's explicit, separate written consent (addendum required).
- Redwood will provide a current subprocessor list and support a customer-specific allowlist for Dedicated or Private deployments. For Hosted customers, Redwood will provide contractual controls plus a mitigation path for new subprocessors.
- Ephemeral KV/cache residency can be limited to us-east with a 30-day TTL; cross-region failover may cause brief replica storage with immediate purge after failover.
- Audit logs will be available with a standard 180-day retention; longer retention can be added via enterprise plan.

Olga will send a clean addendum that incorporates Product's caveats and the final wording. When you confirm that language looks good I will route the addendum to DocuSign (link below) and we can target signature by Friday 1/19.
